stem: Explain why fins are added to heat transfer surfaces, and when adding fins does not help.
rubric: [{"criterion_id": "c1", "text": "States that fins increase the surface area available for convection.", "weight": 2, "layer": "L2", "anchor_pass": "ANCHOR_PASS_MORE_AREA", "anchor_fail": "ANCHOR_FAIL_FINS_INSULATE"}, {"criterion_id": "c2", "text": "Notes that the fin temperature falls along its length, so fin efficiency is below one.", "weight": 1, "layer": "L3"}, {"criterion_id": "c3", "text": "Says fins do not help when the convective coefficient is already high (Biot number near or above one).", "weight": 1, "layer": "L3"}]
model_answer: Fins increase the surface area available for convection, so more heat leaves the wall. The fin temperature falls along its length, so fin efficiency is below one. Fins do not help when the convective coefficient is already high, that is when the Biot number is near or above one.

stem: Size a counter-flow heat exchanger: hot oil cools from 150 C to 90 C, water heats from 30 C to 70 C, duty 50 kW, U = 400 W/(m^2 K). Show your method.
rubric: [{"criterion_id": "c1", "text": "Computes the log-mean temperature difference from the two terminal differences (80 K and 60 K).", "weight": 2, "layer": "L3"}, {"criterion_id": "c2", "text": "Uses Q = U A LMTD to find the area.", "weight": 2, "layer": "L2"}, {"criterion_id": "c3", "text": "Reports an area of about 1.8 m^2 with units.", "weight": 1, "layer": "L5"}]
model_answer: The terminal temperature differences are 150 - 70 = 80 K and 90 - 30 = 60 K, so the log-mean temperature difference is (80 - 60) / ln(80/60) = 69.5 K. Using Q = U A LMTD, A = 50000 / (400 x 69.5) = 1.80 m^2. The required area is about 1.8 m^2.
